To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the semiconducting nature of graphene and other carbon-based electrodes, such as carbon nanotubes, can be eliminated by introducing dopants and/or vacancies.
The quantum capacitance can be enhanced by doping graphene with nitrogen and boron atoms or by creating vacancy defects.

the quantum capacitance can be increased by doping graphene and by introducing vacancy defects that eliminate the Dirac point and that the increase in quantum capacitance leads to an increase in the energy density of supercapacitors containing these doped graphene-based electrodes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new materials and methods to increase the energy storage density of EDL supercapacitors, and with the understanding of the fundamental mechanisms behind these processes.

developing a theoretical framework to design and tailor graphene-based electrodes with the desired electronic properties for energy storage applications, and to understand how these properties affect the performance of EDL capacitors.
the design of new materials that can be used as electrodes in EDL capacitors to increase their energy storage capacity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the energy stored per unit volume in a graphene-based supercapacitor can be increased by a factor of 10–100 by tailoring the graphene structure and electronic properties.
the energy density of the EDL supercapacitor can be increased by tailoring the electronic structure of the graphene electrode to increase its quantum capacitance.

the doping of graphene and the introduction of zigzag edges in carbon-based electrodes can be used to increase the quantum capacitances of the electrodes and, therefore, to increase the energy stored in EDL capacitors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the quantum capacitance is a critical factor in determining the total capacitance and the energy density of graphene and other carbon-based electrodes.
the total capacitance and stored energy density of graphene-based electrodes can be increased by orders of magnitude by tailoring their electronic structure.
the quantum capacitance is a critical factor that should be taken into account in the development of high energy density supercapacitors based on graphene or carbon-based materials.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the energy density of the EDL capacitors can be enhanced by tuning the electronic structure of the electrode materials.
by tailoring the electronic properties of graphene-based electrodes it is possible to increase the stored energy densities of EDL capacitors by a factor of 2–3.

the energy density of the EDL capacitors can be increased significantly by tailoring the electronic structure of the electrode materials, without the need to change the electrolyte or the electrode/electrolyte interface chemistry.
